learningObjectives.title: The causes of the Second World War
The Cold War and the collapse of communism

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.

questions.q: Which article of the Treaty of Versailles forced Germany to accept blame for the war?
questions.explain: Article 231, the 'War Guilt Clause', made Germany accept responsibility for causing the war and justified the reparations.

questions.q: Why did many Germans describe the Treaty of Versailles as a 'diktat'?
options: Because it was written in French
Because Germany was forced to sign terms it had no part in negotiating
Because it was approved by the League of Nations
Because Germany chose its own reparations figure
questions.explain: A 'diktat' means a dictated peace, as Germany was excluded from the talks and had to accept the terms or face invasion.

questions.q: In 1927 the German navy secretly begins building submarines. Which term of the Treaty of Versailles does this violate?
options: The ban on Germany having submarines
The ban on union with Austria
questions.explain: The treaty forbade Germany from having submarines (U-boats), so building them secretly broke the naval restrictions.

questions.q: Why did Clemenceau of France want especially harsh terms imposed on Germany?
options: France had gained little land in the war
France had been invaded by Germany and wanted future security
France wanted to join with Germany economically
France opposed the League of Nations
questions.explain: Having suffered German invasion, France sought to weaken Germany permanently to protect itself from another attack.

questions.q: Where was the headquarters of the League of Nations located?
questions.explain: The League of Nations was based in Geneva, Switzerland, a neutral country.

questions.q: Which major power never joined the League of Nations?
questions.explain: Although President Wilson proposed the League, the US Senate rejected membership and America never joined.

questions.q: How did the absence of the USA weaken the League of Nations?
options: It meant the League had no permanent headquarters
It weakened the impact of economic sanctions and the League's authority
It prevented the League from holding meetings
It stopped Britain and France from joining
questions.explain: Without the world's strongest economy, League sanctions were far less effective and its moral authority was reduced.

questions.q: In which year did Japan invade Manchuria, challenging the League of Nations?
questions.explain: Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931, and the League proved unable to stop it, exposing its weakness.

questions.q: Why did the Abyssinian crisis of 1935-36 damage the League of Nations so badly?
options: Because the League banned all trade with Italy
Because Britain and France acted in their own self-interest rather than stopping Italy
questions.explain: Britain and France secretly negotiated the Hoare-Laval Pact and avoided banning oil, showing they put self-interest above collective security.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler remilitarise the Rhineland?
questions.explain: Hitler sent troops into the demilitarised Rhineland in March 1936, breaking the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.q: What did the Munich Agreement of 1938 give to Hitler?
questions.explain: At Munich, Britain and France agreed to let Germany take the Sudetenland in the hope of preserving peace.

questions.q: In March 1939 German troops occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia, land not promised at Munich. What was the main consequence for British policy?
options: Britain abandoned appeasement and guaranteed to defend Poland
Britain left the League of Nations
Britain signed a pact with the USSR
questions.explain: The seizure of the rest of Czechoslovakia showed appeasement had failed, so Britain guaranteed Polish independence.

questions.q: On what date did Germany invade Poland, triggering the Second World War?
questions.explain: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, leading Britain and France to declare war two days later.

questions.q: Why was the Nazi-Soviet Pact of August 1939 significant in causing war?
options: It formed an alliance against Britain and France for a joint attack
It secretly agreed to divide Poland and freed Hitler to attack without fear of a two-front war
It brought the USA into the conflict
questions.explain: The pact's secret clauses divided Poland and removed the threat of Soviet opposition, so Hitler felt safe to invade.

questions.q: In which year was the Truman Doctrine announced?
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine of 1947 pledged US support to countries resisting communism, a policy of containment.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Marshall Plan?
options: To rearm Germany against the USSR
To give economic aid to rebuild Europe and reduce the appeal of communism
To divide Berlin into four zones
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan offered US financial aid to rebuild Europe, aiming to stop communism spreading in weakened states.

questions.q: In 1948 Stalin cut off all road and rail links to West Berlin. How did the Western powers respond?
options: They supplied the city by air with the Berlin Airlift
questions.explain: The Western Allies flew in supplies for almost a year until Stalin lifted the blockade in 1949.

questions.q: The 1962 crisis over Soviet nuclear missiles on Cuba was ultimately resolved when which of the following happened?
options: The USSR agreed to remove the missiles in return for a US promise not to invade Cuba
questions.explain: Khrushchev withdrew the missiles after the USA pledged not to invade Cuba, ending the crisis peacefully.

questions.q: What did Gorbachev's policy of 'glasnost' mean?
options: Greater openness and freedom of expression
questions.explain: 'Glasnost' meant openness, allowing more freedom of speech and criticism, which helped loosen Soviet control.
